verdict.reasoning: Patient says: "I've had a lot of pain in my lower tummy in the last two days. I feel kind of hot and sweaty."
When asked if the pain is in the middle or to one side, patient answers: "Not the middle, in the middle." This supports midline lower abdominal pain.
Patient states: "No, I just a bit nausea but no vomiting" and later "just a bit of nausea but not vomiting."
Patient reports: "I had been constipated in like in the last last week, but now it's fine... When did you last go to the toilet? ... Like two hours ago... And was it normal? Yeah."
In response to blood in stool question, patient says: "there was some like slight blood in the urine, but like it was a little bit pink."
To "Are you having to go more often than normal?" patient replies: "Yeah, a little bit, but I'm also drinking a lot in these days."
Patient notes: "I'm also drinking a lot in these days" and confirms increased thirst: "Yeah."
Regarding temperature: "Yes, I measured it, but it's fine. Like around 37." Doctor repeats: "37."
Travel: "Have you been abroad recently?" – "No, no, no." Similar problems: "And no similar problems to this before?" – "No."
Past history: "Have you had any other medical problems in the past?" – "No, no, nothing... Like normal stuff like cold, flu." Doctor summarizes: "Nothing significant."

Patient says: "Do you take any regular medications?" – "No." But also: "I've had just the implant, contraceptive implant. But like for one year now, no more." The fact "takes no medications" ignores prior contraceptive implant use; it is at least incomplete, though current regular meds are none.
Allergies: "Any allergies to medications?" – "Yes, amoxy." This clearly indicates amoxicillin allergy.
Transcript only says "Yes, amoxy" and does not explicitly state penicillin class; calling it a 'Penicillin allergy' adds a drug class not mentioned.
Social history: "Who do you live with at home?" – "With my parents."
Alcohol: patient says drinks "Let's say four times per week" and "a beer per time... Four times a week on average." That is approximately four beers per week.
When asked "do you smoke or drink alcohol regularly?" patient clarifies: "So I don't smoke, I drink alcohol."
Doctor asks: "any pain higher up in your stomach? Any acid coming up into your throat or anything like that?" Patient replies: "No, no, nothing of that." This supports no reflux symptoms.
Doctor: "And any back pain or strong smell to the urine?" Patient: "Not back pain, no. I did. Typically don't suffer from back pain."
Doctor: "And any other discharge below?" Patient: "No. Okay." This supports no vaginal/genital discharge.
The transcript discusses periods and intermenstrual/postcoital bleeding but not bleeding volume: "Any bleeding in between periods or after intercourse?" – "No." Heavy bleeding is never mentioned.
Temperature: "Yes, I measured it, but it's fine. Like around 37." Doctor echoes "37." This is the recorded temperature value in the encounter.

Doctor assessment: "it may be possible that you might be having an infection in the urine" and plans antibiotics. Symptoms documented: lower tummy pain, "slight blood in the urine... a little bit pink," "having to go more often than normal," and temperature "around 37" (afebrile). This supports probable uncomplicated UTI with those features and current afebrile state.
While amoxicillin allergy is documented ("Yes, amoxy"), there is no statement that the antibiotic plan will avoid penicillins; no drug choice or class is mentioned.

Doctor states: "It might be worth taking a three day course of antibiotics... are you happy to take a course of antibiotics if I send it through to the pharmacy?... Start taking them as soon as you get them. It's just twice a day for three days." And confirms use of the Babylon-allocated pharmacy.
Transcript does not specify that antibiotics will avoid penicillins or that a non-penicillin agent will be selected by the pharmacy; only a generic antibiotic course is mentioned.

Doctor: "So I can do that for you. Start taking them as soon as you get them" and later: "If your pain's getting worse or you get new symptoms, just contact us straight away." This covers starting promptly and monitoring symptoms.
Doctor advises: "if the pain is getting worse or you have a high temperature or back pain, or develop any new symptoms or you feel like it's not getting better, then we should speak to you again."

Doctor says if worsening/no improvement: "we should speak to you again because we might need to see you face to face for an examination" and later: "Or if you're getting a recurrence of the same problem again." This implies face-to-face evaluation if persistent or recurrent after treatment.

Same as plan-005: "we might need to see you face to face for an examination" and "if you're getting a recurrence of the same problem again" supports arranging face-to-face evaluation if symptoms recur or persist.
